TypeScript adds a static type system on top of JavaScript, letting editors
catch mistakes like calling a function with the wrong argument types before
the code ever runs. When compiled with strict mode enabled, TypeScript
checks nullability, function signatures, and object shapes far more
rigorously than plain JavaScript ever could.

Node.js is a JavaScript runtime built on Chrome's V8 engine that lets
developers run JavaScript outside a web browser, commonly used to build
command-line tools, web servers, and backend services.
